newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PHILIPS CONSUMER PRODUCTS EARNINGS DIP IN Q2.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS CONSUMER PRODUCTS EARNINGS DIP IN Q2.

text.p: Earnings of Philips Electronics NV's core consumer products division declined in the second quarter of 1997 compared with a relatively buoyant performance in the first quarter.
Philips , reporting higher than expected second-quarter earnings on Thursday, did not publish a detailed breakdown of earnings for the second quarter.
But an analysis of first-half figures showed that operating profits from consumer electronics declined to 62 million guilders from 206 million in the first quarter.
Over the first half of 1997 consumer products posted an operating profit of 268 million guilders versus a loss of 92 million in the same period of 1996.
Philips said the consumer products division's first-half sales grew by four percent.

The Sound & Vision business unit -- which makes TV sets, video recorders and CD players -- experienced weak markets in Western Europe and North America, but this was offset by continuing growth in East Europe and the Asia/Pacific region.

Philips said Sound & Vision's first-half results had benefitted from restructuring and the deconsolidation of Grundig -- the loss-making German consumer electronics firm with which Philips has gradually been severing its links.
Results deteriorated at the Consumer Communications phones business -- set up last year -- because of the costs of building up a global organisation and launching new cellular phones.
Philips has recently announced plans to group this business in a joint venture with Lucent Technologies Inc. and has said it will be profitable by October of this year.
Domestic appliances showed a strong improvement in income, Philips added.
